clue.text: Eg Guardian leader in Guardian has got me, but not you, excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so the words in Guardian and got me, but not you, are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letter pool
taken as written, part of the letter pool
you is commonly written as the letter U, as in text messages

explanation.surface: A newspaper's top figure is thrilled by something at the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not you' removes U from the pool IN GUARDIAN GOT ME before 'excited' rearranges the remaining fourteen letters; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The managing editor runs a newspaper's day-to-day business, so is one of its leading figures.

clue.text: See 26
See 1
Passion in forest, city wanting it

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is the woodland setting of As You Like It

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word city loses some of its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds passion in a forest, a city lacking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' signals a removal: the second 'it' is taken from the city, and 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardency is fervour or burning eagerness, a synonym for strong feeling.

clue.text: Creator does without hint

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the deer letters go round the hint

parts.note: does are female deer, so the word stands for deer
a sign is an indication or hint

explanation.surface: A creative person manages without any clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like a verb but is the plural of doe; 'without' is the old sense of outside, an insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A designer devises and creates things such as clothes or products.

clue.text: Dreadful experience on different drug for morning or evening, perhaps

parts.note: hell is a byword for a terrible ordeal
other means different
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A grim time on a new drug, whether in the morning or evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a greeting that can stand in for 'good morning' or 'good evening'; 'on' just places the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a friendly greeting that can replace a time-of-day salutation such as good morning.

clue.text: See 10
Plant that may destroy a toilet?

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory, a toilet
an ender is something that ends or destroys

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about a plant capable of wrecking a loo.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whimsically, the answer is something that ends a lav.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a fragrant shrub with purple flowers, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Chance in card game initially blown

indicators.note: initially blown means the first letter is blown away from the card game's name

parts.note: sevens is a card game in which sevens are laid out first

explanation.surface: Your chances in a card game are ruined right at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVENS is a patience-like card game; 'initially blown' removes its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens is a fifty-fifty probability in betting, an equal likelihood.

clue.text: During safest lap, surprisingly, vehicle at the back crashed out

indicators.note: During says one piece comes in the middle of the other
surprisingly says the letters of safest lap turn up in an unexpected order
at the back picks the final letter of vehicle

explanation.surface: A racing car crashes out during what should have been the safest lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed out' looks like motor racing but is slang for sleeping deeply. The E from 'vehicle at the back' sits within FASTASLP, the anagram of SAFEST LAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To crash out is informal for falling into a deep sleep, so the phrase means sleeping soundly.

clue.text: Having broken marriages, you can rely on him for a creepy feeling

indicators.note: having broken means the reliable fellow has split the ties apart and sits inside them

parts.note: marriages are ties, unions between partners
a dependable man is one of whom you can say he will

explanation.surface: A man you trust after failed marriages gives you the creeps.
explanation.walkthrough: HE WILL, the promise of someone reliable, breaks into TIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The willies is an informal idiom for nervousness or a shudder of unease.

clue.text: See 24
A stuck-up politician, rude

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: stuck with horns means gored
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A snooty politician, rude in manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck-up' looks like snobbish, but splits into a synonym for stuck and 'up', a reversal signal in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogatory remarks are disparaging and insulting, close in sense to impolite.

clue.text: Touch number read as Arabic in church monument

indicators.note: in places the reversed touch-and-number letters inside the church abbreviation
Arabic script runs right to left, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: to pat is to touch lightly
one is a number

explanation.surface: Someone touches an Arabic numeral inscribed on a church memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read as Arabic' reverses PATONE to ENOTAP, which sits inside CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a memorial to the dead buried elsewhere, such as a war memorial.

clue.text: Whip up and turn over US snack

parts.note: to egg on is to whip up or urge
to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: Instructions for beating and flipping something to make an American snack.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg roll is a deep-fried filled pastry, an American name for a spring roll.

clue.text: Tool, visibly sore, covered in soap

parts.note: a lathe is a machine tool for shaping wood or metal
skin that is visibly sore looks red

explanation.surface: A tool, and someone's raw skin, coated in suds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lathered describes being covered in foam from soap or shaving cream.

clue.text: What might secure bottom, but not one side

parts.note: arse is British slang for the bottom

indicators.note: but not means the following item is omitted

parts.note: a nail is something that fastens or secures
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A mysterious device to fasten one's bottom, minus one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' looks like part of the surface but is a team; ARSENAL is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a side is a team, and Arsenal is a famous football team.

clue.text: Bird entertained by boy in garden, holder of massive flower

indicators.note: entertained by means held within, as a guest is within a house

parts.note: Adam was the man in the Garden of Eden
a swan is a bird

explanation.surface: A boy in a garden hosts a bird and holds a huge bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is read as 'flow-er', a river: the dam holds back the Nile. 'massive flower' is not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aswan Dam in Egypt holds back the Nile, a huge river, here a thing that flows.

clue.text: Science a little bit grisly, ultimately

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, a variant of a
an atom is a tiny particle or bit

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of grisly

explanation.surface: A science that is just slightly gruesome in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy is the branch of biology studying bodily structure, a science that can be grisly.

clue.text: Seaside location, sunny and happening

parts.note: bright weather is sunny
an event that is on is happening

explanation.surface: A lively, sun-drenched resort.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a resort town on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a well-known resort town on the English Channel coast.

clue.text: Fancy sauce

definitions.meaning: to fancy is to like or enjoy
a condiment or tangy accompaniment such as chutney

explanation.surface: An elaborate dressing for food.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to enjoy greatly; as a noun it is a tangy condiment.

clue.text: Footballers' exchange covered by radio network

indicators.note: covered by means the letters are concealed within the words radio network

explanation.surface: A passing move in football gets coverage on a radio network.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-two is a quick give-and-go pass between two players, an exchange of the ball.

clue.text: Dropping yellow, German artist unfinished

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold or yellow

indicators.note: unfinished means the artist's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and engraver

explanation.surface: A German painter abandons an unfinished work done in yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' looks like a verb but is a noun, animal dung.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordure is excrement, and a dropping is a lump of animal dung.

clue.text: Dear little cuckoo harmed

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters of dear little go wild

explanation.surface: A sweet young cuckoo has been hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuckoo' looks like the bird but means mad, signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ill-treated is to be abused or mistreated, so hurt.

clue.text: Double locks in attempt to secure new file

indicators.note: locks in means encloses, so the double surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a ringer is a lookalike, as in a dead ringer

indicators.note: to secure means to hold, so the attempt holds the next letter inside

parts.note: a bid is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone tries doubling the locks to protect a new file.
explanation.walkthrough: BID holding N gives BIND, then RINGER locks it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring binder is a folder with metal rings for holding papers, a type of file.

clue.text: Protest about method of travel

explanation.surface: Objecting to a form of transport.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to complain loudly; as a noun it means the railway as a mode of transport.

clue.text: Copper river in shade of green?

indicators.note: in places the river abbreviation inside the colour word

parts.note: sage is a greyish-green colour

explanation.surface: A copper-coloured river among shades of green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like the metal or colour but is slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarge is short for sergeant, a police rank, and a copper is a police officer.

clue.text: French victim of assassination pierced by a single shot — political target?

indicators.note: pierced by means the next piece goes through the middle of the revolutionary's name

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat, French revolutionary, was stabbed in his bath

indicators.note: shot means broken up, so the letters of a single are scrambled

explanation.surface: A French revolutionary killed by a single shot, a political target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' scrambles A SINGLE into GINALSE, which pierces MARAT. Marat was in fact stabbed, not shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A marginal seat is a constituency with a slim majority, which parties target in elections.
